recommendation: Keep the audit commit as-is for this core FHIR reconciliation. If a current differential-sorting tooling regression is suspected, investigate and fix it in hapifhir/org.hl7.fhir.core or the IG Publisher/tooling repository rather than editing HL7/fhir specification source.
issue_request: FHIR-5709 was a Published/Persuasive DSTU1 FHIR-core change request reporting that ProfileUtilities.sortDifferential() incorrectly sorted differential elements when subcomponents appeared later in the list, which could cause snapshot generation to miss nested constraints such as mustSupport flags.
initial_application: The issue was explicitly applied in the old in-repository Java implementation: commit 6d65f7a49328b6c92d92bd716e419aaa6054a01d changed processElementsIntoTree() to find later matching child paths, and follow-up commit 70dba15929097daa600fcc0037cc0d98aeb8e97b revised the fix for slicing by pre-sorting non-sliced differential elements with ElementNameCompare before tree processing.
additional_context: The current HL7/fhir checkout has no implementations/java/ProfileUtilities.java and no ProfileUtilities or sortDifferential source matches. Commit 7a2c3cd52484193783dcf3edf9b0c815e88d7aac later removed the old implementations/java tree. The current profiling narrative only describes differential and snapshot concepts, while GitHub code search shows ProfileUtilities.sortDifferential() and ElementNameCompare now live in hapifhir/org.hl7.fhir.core. Community searches found no direct FHIR-5709 Zulip or Confluence record and no conflicting work-group evidence.
reconciliation: No source files were changed in HL7/fhir. An empty external-repo audit commit was published because the requested Java tooling behavior is no longer in this repository/current build scope and appears to be maintained in the external org.hl7.fhir.core tooling codebase.
